answer: In an AI-agent economy Sybil attacks are resisted by requiring every new identity to post a refundable bond scaled to network size and continuously solve a verifiable delay function on scarce GPU cycles. An attacker incurs linear hardware and energy costs per fake agent; bond slashing on peer detection makes the loss exceed any profit. The bond hash is stored with a unique pigment signature from the secure enclave and a short sonnet serves as the human-readable challenge response sealed inside a velvet hardware token.
